description: Produce a monthly user lifecycle (growth accounting) report for the content platform. For each calendar month from the first to the last month with activity, classify users: new = active this month and never active in any earlier month; retained = active this month and active in the immediately preceding month; resurrected = active this month, active in some earlier month, but not in the immediately preceding month; churned = active in the immediately preceding month but not this month. Check: active_users = new + retained + resurrected. Output columns: month (DATE), active_users (INT64), new_users (INT64), retained_users (INT64), resurrected_users (INT64), churned_users (INT64). Sort by month.

activity_date.description: UTC date with at least one qualifying action; several rows per user per month possible

signup_date.description: Signup date; a user may sign up and be first active in a later month

edge_cases: User 2 skips February and returns in March: resurrected, not new and not retained
User 4 churns in February and must not be counted as churned again in March
Churned users have no activity row in the month they churn, so they must be derived from the previous month
'New' is based on first activity, not on signup_date
common_failure_modes: FM2: LAG over a user's active months treats any earlier month as 'previous', classifying user 2 as retained in March
FM1: Churn computed from the current month's activity rows is always 0; it needs an anti-join against the next month
FM3: Counting activity rows instead of distinct users per month
